Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Next steps: SDK auth pattern + service-account handoff (QuantifyHealth)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can unblock your infra team:

Summary from today's call
- Goal: integrate Redwood inference into QuantifyHealth's chart summarization pipeline (embedding + reranker + structured tool-calls for diagnosis lookup).
- Main asks: recommend a secure auth pattern for service-to-service calls, guidance for key rotation, and SDK init examples for short-lived tokens.

Proposed authentication approach (high level)
1) Preferred: Customer-managed service account with short-lived JWTs issued by your IdP -> exchange for Redwood access token (OAuth2 token exchange). This avoids long-lived API keys stored in app configs.
2) Alternative (fast path for PoC): Scoped API key with strict IP egress + host-level secret store (only for sandbox, not recommended for prod).

We suggest the following immediate items (actionable):
- QuantifyHealth infra to spin up a service account for the PoC and grant it a narrow role (token-exchange). (Alice / infra)
- Redwood to provide a short README + SDK snippet for token exchange + minimum scopes required. (Neha / Marissa)
- Security sync: share the list of evidence you need (KMS/HSM, rotation logs, audit window). (Alice / procurement contact)

Attachments: I attached a short checklist (qh-key-ops-checklist.pdf) and an SDK init snippet file. Ben also added a checklist with rotation recommendations.

If that plan sounds good I can schedule a 30 min sync between your infra/security and Ben next week. Proposed times: Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@quantifyhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 18:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK auth pattern + service-account handoff (QuantifyHealth)

Hi Alice — quick answers and a lightweight ops checklist attached. TL;DR answers:

1) JWT expectations: Standard RFC7523 is fine. Include aud: "https://api.redwood.com/token-exchange" and exp/leeway similar to your policy. We need a subject claim (sub) with the service account id.

2) Single service account is okay for PoC if you use role-based scoping (ingest vs runtime flag in claims) — for prod we recommend separating identities for ingestion (data write) and runtime (inference calls) to reduce blast radius.

3) Rotation cadence: PoC -> rotate every 90 days is acceptable; Prod -> recommend short-lived keys with automated rotation every 7–30 days depending on criticality. We support both HSM-backed key material and rotated symmetric keys via KMS.

Attached: qh-key-ops-checklist.pdf (ops steps + sample IAM policy), redwood-sdk-init-snippet.txt (node/python examples for token-exchange + SDK init).

Sample minimal SDK init (pseudo):
```
// token is acquired from your IdP, exchanged at Redwood token-exchange endpoint
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  token: process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN,
  region: 'us-west-2',
  enableStructuredOutput: true, // for tool-calling
});
```
If you want I can join the sync to walk through the sample and runtime routing options (regional model pinning vs. fallback).

-ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
